strategy.bottleneck: [compute-bound mainloop + bandwidth-bound aux pass] The conv segment dominates: cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop_tf32 = 79.2% (742 us/conv ≈ 99.5% of the 738 us TF32 roofline for 77.3 GFLOP), so the mainloop is untouchable. But cuDNN emits 48 convertTensor_kernel launches (7.3%, 1646 us; 2 per conv ≈ one full 67 MB activation copy each) — a pure fp32→tf32 pre-rounding pass adding ~268 MB/iteration of DRAM traffic.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: cuDNN engine/algo re-selection: call the convolutions through at::cudnn_convolution with benchmark=true (cudnnFind-style plan search) instead of heuristic-mode at::conv2d, so the engine is chosen by measured end-to-end time including its auxiliary kernels. Engines that fold the tf32 conversion in-kernel then win over the pre-compiled engine that needs a separate full-tensor convertTensor prologue, deleting ~268 MB/iteration of read+write traffic without touching the roofline-limited mainloop or precision (TF32, as reference).

Alternative bottleneck refuted: the cutlass fprop mainloop is NOT improvable — 17812 us/24 = 742 us per conv vs 738 us theoretical at 104.8 TF32 TFLOPS (77.3 GFLOP/conv) = 99.5% of roofline; likewise the five custom kernels already run at 81.5–90% DRAM peak (gpu__dram_throughput 86.7/81.7/81.5/90.0%), so they hold <10% recoverable time.

strategy.bottleneck: [latency/serialization] The two cuDNN TF32 conv kernels (47.9% GPU time, ~761 µs each ≈ 101 of 104.8 TFLOPS) are compute-bound and leave DRAM ~11% idle, while the five custom kernels (nchw2nhwc 72 µs, gn_partial 2×47 µs, gn_silu_inplace 70 µs, gn_silu_res_nchw 114 µs = 357 µs/iter) are DRAM-bound at 86–90% of peak with sm__throughput 6–19%. Complementary resources, but strictly serialized.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Batch-chunked two-stream pipelining: GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-image, so the whole block splits exactly along N. Run the full chain per batch chunk on 2 alternating CUDA streams so chunk i's memory-bound GN/transpose/SiLU kernels (86–90% DRAM, 6–19% SM) co-execute with chunk i+1's tensor-core conv (near-peak SM, 11% DRAM). Hides most of the 357 µs/iter of bandwidth work under 1522 µs of conv compute; smaller chunks also raise L2 reuse.

If `nchunk==1`, execute exactly today's code path unchanged (protects the 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 shapes).

(Exact rewrite) Wrap the existing body in `for (int ci=0; ci<nchunk; ++ci)` operating on N-slices: `auto xc_c = xc.narrow(0, ci*cb, cb); auto out_c = out.narrow(0, ci*cb, cb);` and pass `cb` as the batch to every kernel (grid.z = cb, buffers sized cb). NHWC/NCHW batch slices stay contiguous, so all pointer arithmetic is unchanged. Keep `calc_pix_per_block(HW, B_full)` (full B, not cb) so gn_partial's per-image reduction order — hence the bitwise result — is identical to today.

Per chunk: `c10::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(S[ci & 1]);` around the whole chunk body so ATen conv output allocations, cuDNN handle stream and all 5 custom kernels (launch with `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()`) run on that stream. Within a chunk everything stays sequential → dependencies preserved.

strategy.optimisation method: Capture the entire ModelNew.forward (weight relayout + 5 custom kernels + both cuDNN convs, incl. the two-stream fork/join) once per input shape into a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph over static input/output buffers, then replay: one graph launch replaces ~172 launches per call, removing per-launch dispatch and inter-kernel gaps.
strategy.modification plan:
1. In ModelNew.__init__ add: self._graphs = {} (cache), self._pool = None (shared torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle(), created lazily), self._graph_ok = True (sticky disable on failure).
2. Build a cache key in forward: (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device.index, tuple(conv1_weight.shape), tuple(conv2_weight.shape), eps_f). This keys all four benchmark shapes separately so each gets its own graph; no recapture for a repeated shape.
3. On cache miss and self._graph_ok and x.is_cuda and use_fast: call self._capture(key, x, w1, g1, b1, w2, g2, b2, eps_f) inside try/except; on any exception set self._graph_ok=False and fall through to today's eager `self._ext.fused_resblock(...)` path.
4. _capture: allocate static buffers with fixed addresses — static_x = torch.empty_like(x).contiguous(); static_w1, static_g1, static_b1, static_w2, static_g2, static_b2 = torch.empty_like(t).contiguous() for each parameter tensor; copy the current values into all of them with .copy_() BEFORE warmup.
5. Warmup (mandatory, outside capture) on a dedicated side stream: s = torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream()); with torch.cuda.stream(s): run self._cl_weight(static_w1/static_w2) and self._ext.fused_resblock(static_x, w1c, static_g1, static_b1, w2c, static_g2, static_b2, eps_f) three times; torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s); torch.cuda.synchronize(). This forces cuDNN benchmark autotuning, workspace allocation, the channels_last weight relayout into self._cl_cache (keyed by id(static_w*), which is now stable), and the one-time init_cudnn_flags — so the capture region performs NO algorithm search.
6. Capture: if self._pool is None: self._pool = torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle(); g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(); with torch.cuda.graph(g, pool=self._pool): static_out = self._ext.fused_resblock(static_x, self._cl_weight(static_w1), static_g1, static_b1, self._cl_weight(static_w2), static_g2, static_b2, eps_f). Keep the returned static_out tensor alive in the cache entry (its storage lives in the graph pool and is address-stable across replays). Sharing one pool across the four shape-graphs bounds extra memory.
7. Multi-stream safety: the extension's fork/join (CUDAEvent record on main stream, block on the two pool side streams, events back to main) is capture-legal, but add a defensive retry — extend fused_resblock with a trailing `bool force_single_stream=false` argument that forces nchunk=1/cb=B; if the first capture throws, delete the graph and retry capture once with force_single_stream=true; if that also throws, set self._graph_ok=False.
8. Replay path (cache hit): static_x.copy_(x, non_blocking=True) and .copy_() the six parameter tensors into their static buffers (cheap: weights are 2.36 MB each, x-copy is the only sizeable one), then graph.replay(), then return static_out. No allocation, no .item(), no device query, no stream switch on this path.
9. eps handling stays as today (float(eps.item()) once per call before the key is built); eps is baked into the captured kernels, and since it is part of the cache key a different eps forces a fresh capture.
10. Keep every kernel body, block size, grid shape and numerics unchanged — this round only removes launch/dispatch overhead. Keep the existing fallback branches (non-CUDA, non-fp32, C!=256) routed to the eager PyTorch path untouched.
11. Do not modify get_inputs/get_init_inputs, do not move tensors across devices, and allocate static buffers on x.device.

strategy.bottleneck: [memory/DRAM-bound epilogue chain]. The cutlass TF32 fprop mainloop holds 69.1% but is already at vendor SOL (~103 TFLOPS on 4x256x256x256 vs 104.8 TF32 peak) → default-keep. The addressable 31% is the GN/layout chain (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial x2, gn_silu_inplace, gn_silu_res), all DRAM-bound with ~77-95% long-scoreboard stalls and near-zero L2 reuse although each chunk buffer is touched 3-4 times.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: L2 cache-residency control (reuse, not new math): pin the per-chunk activation buffer (conv output y / y2, 8-17 MB on three of four shapes) in L2 with a cudaAccessPolicyWindow (hitProp=persisting, missProp=streaming) on the owning stream, plus persist-aware chunk sizing. The stats pass, the normalize+SiLU pass and conv2's input read then hit L2 instead of DRAM. Justified by E1: gn_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate=1.59% and gn_silu_res=1.96% while both sit at 73-87% DRAM peak with 94.9%/78.0% long-scoreboard stalls.
strategy.modification_plan:
1. EXACT CODE ACTION (setup): add `static size_t g_persist_max=0, g_win_max=0;` and `static void init_l2_persist(){ cudaDeviceProp p; int d; cudaGetDevice(&d); if(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&p,d)==cudaSuccess){ g_persist_max=p.persistingL2CacheMaxSize; g_win_max=p.accessPolicyMaxWindowSize; if(g_persist_max) cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, g_persist_max);} }` and call it inside the existing `init_cudnn_flags()` once-lambda (single global init, no per-call cost).

EXACT CODE ACTION (window helpers): add `static void set_persist(cudaStream_t s, const void* p, size_t bytes, int nact){ if(!g_persist_max) return; size_t budget=g_persist_max/(size_t)std::max(1,nact); size_t win=std::min(bytes, g_win_max?g_win_max:bytes); float r=(float)budget/(float)win; if(r>1.f) r=1.f; if(r<0.25f){ clear_persist(s); return;} cudaStreamAttrValue v{}; v.accessPolicyWindow.base_ptr=(void*)p; v.accessPolicyWindow.num_bytes=win; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitRatio=r; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitProp=cudaAccessPropertyPersisting; v.accessPolicyWindow.missProp=cudaAccessPropertyStreaming; cudaStreamSetAttribute(s, cudaStreamAttributeAccessPolicyWindow, &v);} ` and `clear_persist(s)` identical but with `num_bytes=0, hitProp=missProp=cudaAccessPropertyNormal`. Immediately after conv1 and its channels_last check: `set_persist(stream, y.data_ptr<float>(), (size_t)Bc*C*HW*4, nact);` and leave the window installed across gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace AND conv2, so conv2's read of y is also served from L2.

The filter transform is loop-invariant yet re-executed every forward call.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Vendor conv invocation-plan caching + filter prepack: pick, once per input shape and cache, the (filter layout, cuDNN entry point, conv invocations per forward) combination by real cudaEvent timing, then reuse a pre-packed filter tensor on every subsequent call. This removes the per-call loop-invariant filter conversion (232 convertTensor launches, 4.8% of GPU time doing zero math) and lets cuDNN benchmark a wider engine set on larger per-call M, addressing the ~15% gap between measured conv time (9.38ms/iter) and TF32 roofline (7.94ms/iter).

Pass a `const at::Tensor&` chosen by the cached plan into `at::cudnn_convolution`, so no filter re-materialisation or re-transform is requested per call.
